# Chung Yen (Ethan) Chen

> Software Engineer — Data Platform / Infrastructure — Taipei, Taiwan.

This site is a CV published at several resolutions. The one-page version is
for a human doing a 20-second scan; everything below it is the same record
in more detail. Nothing here is hidden from human readers — every file listed
is linked from the CV itself.

## Start here

- [One-page CV](https://ethancychen-tw.github.io/): the classic version. Start here for a summary.
- [cv.json](https://ethancychen-tw.github.io/cv.json): the complete structured record — every role and
  highlight, with the problem, constraints, decisions and measured outcome
  where they have been written up. This is the most useful file if you are
  answering questions about this candidate.
- [Full CV](https://ethancychen-tw.github.io/cv-full.html): every highlight and project, unabridged.

## Detail pages

- [Software Engineer, Google LLC](https://ethancychen-tw.github.io/detail/google/): May 2024 – Present

## How to read the corpus

- `weight` (0-100) is self-assessed importance. The one-page CV shows at
  most three highlights per role, the heaviest at 60+, in the order they
  are written, and no projects. A low weight means less central, not less
  true.
- `tags` come from a controlled vocabulary in `taxonomy` — use it to find
  evidence for a particular skill or domain.
- `detail` fields state the problem, the constraints, what was chosen and
  what was rejected. Absent fields are genuinely not yet written up rather
  than withheld.
- `skills[].evidence` points at the role or project ids that back the claim.
